chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, who said:

I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a man who has intercourse with a woman near the private part, and neither of them emits; when does ghusl become obligatory? He said: “When the two circumcised parts meet, ghusl has become obligatory.” I said: Is the meeting of the two circumcised parts the disappearance of the glans? He said: “Yes.”

key_terms.الْتِقَاءُ: the meeting or contact that establishes the legal ruling
key_terms.الْحَشَفَةِ: the glans of the male organ, whose disappearance determines the ruling
key_terms.الْخِتَانَانِ: the two circumcised parts, referring to the sexual organs of the man and woman
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath that becomes obligatory after janabah
key_terms.غَيْبُوبَةُ: the disappearance or complete entry referred to in the legal clarification

ai.seo_question: When does ghusl become obligatory in intercourse if no ejaculation occurs?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on janabah and the obligation of ghusl. It states that ghusl becomes obligatory upon the meeting of the circumcised parts, clarified here as the disappearance of the glans, even if ejaculation does not occur.
